title: Mortara wins Norisring Race 1 from pole as Paffett takes the points lead
dek: Edoardo Mortara converted pole into victory for Silberpfeil Energy Mercedes-AMG, 0.681 seconds clear of Gary Paffett, who took the championship lead, while Audi finished outside the top ten.

chapters.title: The street circuit with a tight title race
text: The DTM reached the Norisring for the weekend of 22–24 June with the title fight wide open. The first six races of 2018 had produced five different winners, and the previous round at the Hungaroring had split the spoils: Paul di Resta won Race 1 from pole for Mercedes-AMG, and Marco Wittmann won Race 2 for BMW after starting 14th. Timo Glock arrived as the championship leader in his BMW Team RMR car, with Paffett and di Resta among his closest rivals.

Nuremberg is the only street circuit on the DTM calendar, a 2.3-kilometre loop around the Dutzendteich lake lined with walls. That puts a premium on qualifying and on the timing of the mandatory pit stop and tyre change, one of the few strategic levers in a 55-minute sprint. Race 1 was the seventh round of a 20-race season.

The weekend carried a strong home flavour for BMW. Wittmann, a two-time champion and the local favourite, had never stood on the podium at his home race. Audi came with defending champion René Rast and a car that had been struggling for pace against Mercedes-AMG and BMW.

chapters.title: Pole by one thousandth of a second
text: Saturday morning’s qualifying was settled by the narrowest of margins. Edoardo Mortara put his Silberpfeil Energy Mercedes-AMG on pole with a 47.843, and BMW rookie Philipp Eng, in the second Team RMR car, was only 0.001 seconds slower on 47.844. Wittmann was third on 47.866, delighting the home crowd, and Gary Paffett completed a 47.872 for fourth, the top four covered by 0.029 seconds.

Paul di Resta (47.899) and Daniel Juncadella (47.919) made up the third row, all-Mercedes, ahead of Lucas Auer (47.934). Championship leader Glock could manage only eighth on 47.950 and was behind both of his closest title rivals, Paffett and di Resta. Bruno Spengler was ninth for BMW Team RBM.

It was another difficult session for Audi. Nico Müller was the best of the marque in tenth on 48.067, and the rest of the Audi contingent filled the rear of the grid. René Rast, the reigning champion, spun into the wall at the Schöller-S and damaged the car, which left him last of the 18 runners, 0.601 seconds off Mortara’s pole time. The session was interrupted after the accident.

chapters.title: Mortara holds the lead as the stops begin
text: Mortara kept the lead through the first corners even though Eng had made the slightly better getaway. Eng then came into the pits at the end of the opening lap for his stop, and Wittmann inherited second place, the only non-Mercedes driver in the top five. Di Resta passed Paffett on the first lap to run third, with Auer next.

The first pit stops arrived almost immediately. Juncadella, Müller and Loïc Duval were among the cars to come in after one lap, and Rast followed a lap later after his long climb from the back. The leaders waited, with Mortara a little more than half a second ahead of Wittmann in the early laps. Wittmann stopped on lap 7 and Mortara covered him a lap or two later, emerging still ahead of the BMW.

chapters.title: Paffett works his way past Wittmann
text: Paffett had passed di Resta before stopping and rejoined around lap 12, fresh tyres under him, close to Mortara and Wittmann. Mortara moved back ahead of his team-mate at Turn 1, but the BMW, with its tyres in better shape, also passed the Mercedes on the outside of the Schöller chicane while Paffett’s tyres were still cold.

The front three pulled away from Eng and Juncadella, who were struggling on their older rubber. For much of the middle of the race Wittmann stayed within a second of the leader, but Paffett, who had been fastest of the three, took second from him into Turn 1 with about 20 minutes left, around lap 45. That gave Mercedes a one-two and put Paffett in the position to chase Mortara for the win.

chapters.title: Paffett presses, Mortara holds on
text: Paffett pushed Mortara hard in the final laps and got alongside him at Turn 1 once, but could not make a move stick, and had little left to attack with. Mortara kept the lead to the flag after 68 laps in 56 minutes 12.918 seconds, taking his second win of the season, 0.681 seconds ahead of Paffett.

Wittmann was 1.286 seconds behind in third and took his first podium finish in his home race. Di Resta was a distant fourth, 8.550 seconds back, after passing Eng, who held fifth from Spengler, Auer and Juncadella. Juncadella set the fastest lap, a 48.307 on lap 7. Joel Eriksson and Glock took ninth and tenth. Jamie Green’s eleventh place was the best an Audi could manage, and Robin Frijns, twelfth, ran a long first stint and made his stop late in the race.

Paffett’s second place was enough to take the championship lead on 97 points, six clear of Glock on 91. Mortara won in a car painted in the German national football team’s livery on the day Germany played at the World Cup, and no Audi finished in the top ten.

facts.v: Mortara took pole with a 47.843 at the Norisring, only 0.001 seconds ahead of BMW rookie Philipp Eng, with Wittmann third.
